newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH REFINERIES UP PETROL PRICES.
newsitem.headline: POLISH REFINERIES UP PETROL PRICES.

text.p: Poland's oil refineries on Friday announced 20-30 zloty a tonne increases in the wholesale price of gasoline.
Petrochemia Plock spokeswoman Romana Kuffel said the company will increase gasoline prices from Monday by 20 zlotys a tonne, but will not raise the price of diesel.
The smaller Gdansk refinery earlier announced a 30 zloty a tonne rise.
The rise could translate into an increase of retail petrol prices of about 0.02 zloty per litre.
Kuffel said the increase, already the third since July, resulted from high world oil prices and the increasingly strong U.S. dollar.
The Gdansk refinery's 30 zlotys a tonne increase in both petrol and diesel cost from Monday follows an increase of 20 zlotys a tonne on Wednesday.
Since July Gdansk and Plock, which supply 80 percent of the Polish market, have increased prices by between 0.02 and 0.05 zloty a litre, depending on petrol brand.
Analysts said the increases in the wholesale cost had not yet been fully reflected in retail prices, which they expected to start growing next week.
Poland's petrol prices have increased by between five and 13 percent since the government freed them in February.
